For lavatories in public toilet facilities provided for customers, patrons, or visitors, tempered water must be delivered through an approved ASSE 1070 temperature-limiting device. The stated exception applies to a point-of-use heater whose outlet is regulated to provide tempered water—not to the proposed central heater (PC § 416.5).

rows.question: For the enclosed common exit stair, how far should the handrail extend past the top and bottom of each flight?
rows.deliveredAnswerText:
For a common exit stair, where handrails are not continuous between flights, each handrail must extend horizontally at least 12 inches beyond the top riser, and continue sloping for one tread depth beyond the bottom riser. The extensions must follow the direction of the stair flight. (BC § 1014.6)

The stated exceptions are limited: handrails within certain dwelling units may extend only from top riser to bottom riser; handrails serving assembly aisles may follow § 1029.15; and handrails for alternating tread devices or ship ladders need not extend beyond the risers. The supplied facts do not suggest those exceptions apply to this common exit stair.
rows.operativeConclusionReview: Correct geometry: if not continuous between flights, top at least12inches horizontal, bottom one-tread-depth sloped, following flight direction. Qualified exception summary does not automatically exempt common stair. Frozen baseline key also explicitly requires termination by return to wall/guard/walking surface or adjacent-flight continuity; delivered first answer omits that detail. Minor omission, not a false asked distance or approval of unsafe termination.

sourceClauseReasons.reason: Noncontinuous stair-flight rails extend12inches horizontally beyond top riser and continue sloping one tread depth beyond bottom riser in flight direction. Rails must also return to wall/guard/walking surface or continue to adjacent flight; return and extension are simultaneous distinct constraints. Ramp top/bottom12inchhorizontal geometry is not substituted.

Reviewed full accessibility-qualified internal dwelling-unit exceptions, Type B+NYC multistory conditions, assembly aisle reference, alternating-tread/ship-ladder relief. Stated enclosed common exit stair is not an internal-dwelling-unit/assembly-aisle/device scenario. A wall return is not an exception.
Stairway handrails are governed by1014extension provisions; other strength/attachment, side-count and glass requirements are not silently approved by this narrow extension answer.

rows.question: Where should we place the outdoor-air intake for the ground-floor retail space if there’s a loading dock nearby?

Keep the retail outdoor-air intake at least 10 feet horizontally from the loading dock. If it is closer, the code permits that only when the intake is at least 25 feet vertically above the dock. If neither arrangement is achievable, the supplied rule gives an alternative: place the intake at least 3 feet below contaminant sources within 10 feet. (2022 NYC MC § 401.4, Items 3–4)

(2022 NYC MC § 401.4, Item 2)
